description: The discourse rules as GRAPH DATA (the jabberwock's spec: 'control words are read by seeded discourse rules into control-structure nodes'). Two tables of NODES — the connective->plan-node mapping and the preposition->role mapping — plus bind_role as ONE seeded RULE. The connectives/mappings/binding live here as graph data, NOT hardcoded in a Python parser: adding a connective, a role-preposition, or changing the binding is adding/editing a node, never editing code. A generic interpreter reads these tables (the verb->primitive map already lives on the enact seed's OperationPrimitive `verbs` attr).

attrs.comment: X then Y -> Seq([X,Y]); satisfaction = sat(last)
(repeatedly) B until P -> Fix(guard=P, body=B); satisfaction = guard
while P, B -> Fix(NOT P, B)
if P then X [else Y] -> Branch(P,X,Y); satisfaction = sat(taken)

rules.name: bind_role
rules.comment: ONE seeded rule (the jabberwock's spec): bind each role-filler to the entity its Mention refers_to. This REUSES the agent's existing referent-resolution (Mention -> refers_to -> the resolved entity, the selectional-match family). The role rides on the RoleFiller node; the binding is rf -filled_by-> e. No per-domain code, no Python parser branch — a join over refers_to.
